newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Adria Airways sees bigger 96 net loss.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Adria Airways sees bigger 96 net loss.

text.p: Slovenia's only airline Adria Airways said on Wednesday it expected its 1996 net loss to widen to $8.0 million from $7.8 million in 1995 because of higher debt payments.
Turnover fell to $97 million from $112.2 million. Adria said 1995 turnover was boosted by the sale of two planes.

Adria said it had a debt of $51.3 million at the end of the 1996. The airline began accumulating debts in 1991 when it was forced to halt operations for five months because of the break-up of the former Yugoslavia.
The company then also lost its main markets -- the other states of the former Yugoslavia.
Adria said it would restart flying to Sarajevo on March 3, four times a week with a 46-seat De Havilland Canada Dash 7 aircraft.
Currently Adria has a fleet of seven aircraft comprising three Airbus A320, two McDonnell-Douglas DC9 and two De Havilland Canada Dash 7.

The company had already reported its passenger traffic in 1996 rose by nine percent to 594,000, while cargo volume decreased by two percent to 3,785 tonnes. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
